title: 03-periodicity-recurrence
text:
2.4 Define functions
Runs a periodogram for one block and returns the fit object.


Code
fit_lomb <- function(hrs, resid, from, to, ofac) {
  to <- min(to, diff(range(hrs)) / 3)   # need >= 3 cycles inside the block
  lsp(x = resid, times = hrs, from = from, to = to,
      type = "period", ofac = ofac, plot = FALSE)
}


Assigns a peak period to a target band.


Code
assign_band <- function(period_h) {
  case_when(
    period_h >= band_table$lo[1] & period_h <= band_table$hi[1] ~ band_table$BAND[1],
    period_h >= band_table$lo[2] & period_h <= band_table$hi[2] ~ band_table$BAND[2],
    period_h >= band_table$lo[3] & period_h <= band_table$hi[3] ~ band_table$BAND[3],
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  )
}

title: 03-periodicity-recurrence
text:
2.5 Fit periodograms for chosen CELL_IDs
Defines a function that fits one periodogram per block for each CELL_ID supplied.


Code
run_lomb_fits <- function(cell_ids) {
  block_data |>
    filter(CELL_ID %in% cell_ids) |>
    select(CELL_ID, SEASON, BLOCK_ID, BLOCK_YEAR, hrs, RESID) |>   # drop columns that would split the groups
    group_by(CELL_ID, SEASON, BLOCK_ID, BLOCK_YEAR) |>
    filter(sd(RESID) > 0) |>                                       # flat series cannot be scanned
    filter(sum(is.finite(RESID)) >= min_obs_fit) |>                # too few points cannot be scanned
    nest(series = c(hrs, RESID)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(fit = map(series, ~ fit_lomb(.x$hrs, .x$RESID, min_period_h, max_period_h, ofac)))
}

lomb_results <- lomb_fits |>
  mutate(
    PEAK_PERIOD_H = map_dbl(fit, ~ .x$scanned[which.max(.x$power)]),  # period of the highest peak

  mutate(BAND = assign_band(PEAK_PERIOD_H))   # multiple-testing correction is done in 03, after all CELL_IDs are combined

Code
season_order <- c("Cool", "Spring freshening", "Hot hypersaline", "Autumn low-inflow")



Addition 1: What are the dominant peaks?
Shows where the dominant peak of each block falls across all periods, and adds bands for synoptic (cold-front, 3-10 d) variability. The original band_table is left unchanged; extended_bands is used only in these additions.


Code
extended_bands <- tribble(
  ~BAND, ~lo, ~hi,
  "Tidal (~12.4 h)", 11.5, 13.5,
  "Diel (24 h)", 22.5, 25.5,
  "Synoptic (3-10 d)", 72, 240,
  "Spring-neap (~14.8 d)", 300, 410
)

assign_band_ext <- function(period_h, bands = extended_bands) {
  idx <- map_int(period_h, \(p) {
    hit <- which(p >= bands$lo & p <= bands$hi)
    if (length(hit)) hit[1] else NA_integer_
  })
  coalesce(bands$BAND[idx], "Other")
}

section: 3.2 Hourly to weekly bins by year
text:
3.2 Hourly to weekly bins by year
Hourly environmental records are collapsed to one value per year and day-of-year bin. All parameters are averaged over the sampled hours; precipitation is the mean hourly rate scaled to inches per day (IFCB sampling is not continuous, so a sum over sampled hours would be biased).


Code
env_hourly <- counts_seasonal_metadata_clean |>
  select(DAY, YEAR, doy, all_of(names(env_labels))) |>
  distinct() |> # counts are in long format, so collapse to one row per hour
  mutate(doy = pmin(doy, 365), # fold leap day into Dec 31
         bin = (doy - 1) %/% bin_days + 1, # 1 = Jan 1-7, etc.
         discharge_cfs = discharge_cfs / 1000)

title: 02-overview-seasonality-stats
text:
3.3 Mean and spread across years


Code
env_clim <- env_year_bin |>
  group_by(name, bin) |>
  summarise(n_years = n_distinct(YEAR),
            mean = mean(value),
            sd = sd(value),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(se = sd / sqrt(n_years),
         spread = if (band_type == "se") se else sd) |>
  right_join(expand_grid(name = names(env_labels), bin = 1:ceiling(365 / bin_days)),
             by = c("name", "bin")) |> # add empty rows so gaps are explicit
  mutate(missing = is.na(mean) | n_years < min_years_bin,
         across(c(mean, sd, se, spread), ~ if_else(missing, NA_real_, .x)),
         x_doy = (bin - 1) * bin_days + (bin_days + 1) / 2, # bin midpoint
         name = factor(name, levels = names(env_labels)))

Season color bar
A single bar spanning the same day-of-year axis as the panels below.


Code
season_bar <- ggplot(season_rects) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = 0, ymax = 1, fill = season),
            colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  # geom_text(data = season_rects |> group_by(season) |> slice_max(xmax - xmin, n = 1), # label the longest piece of a wrapped season
            # aes(x = (xmin + xmax) / 2, y = 0.5, label = season),
            # colour = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, 365.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = season_pal, guide = "none") +
  theme_void()


Solid lines are runs of consecutive bins; the dashed line bridges bins with missing data.


Code
env_runs <- env_clim |>
  arrange(name, bin) |>
  group_by(name) |>
  mutate(run = cumsum(missing)) |> # a new run starts after each missing bin
  ungroup() |>
  filter(!missing)




Define environmental panels


Code
env_panels <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = filter(season_rects, shade),
            aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, 
                ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = "grey92") +
  # RIBBON for spread
  geom_ribbon(data = env_runs,
              aes(x = x_doy, ymin = if_else(name == "PRECIP_in", pmax(mean - spread, 0), mean - spread), # stop at 0
                  ymax = mean + spread,
                  group = interaction(name, run)),
              fill = "grey20", alpha = 0.4) +
  # Get NAs filled in with dash. shows gaps
  geom_line(data = env_runs, 
            aes(x = x_doy, y = mean),
            linetype = "dashed", 
            color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = env_runs, aes(x = x_doy, y = mean, group = interaction(name, run)),
            color = "black", linewidth = 0.7) + # solid where consecutive bins exist
  geom_point(data = storm_points,
             aes(x = x_doy, y = value, fill = storm_type),
             shape = 21, color = "white", stroke = 0.4, size = 3, alpha = 0.9) +
  facet_grid(name ~ ., scales = "free_y", switch = "y",
             labeller = labeller(name = env_labels)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = month_starts + 14, labels = month.abb,
                     limits = c(0.5, 365.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = storm_pal, name = "Storm type", drop = FALSE) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
  labs(x = "", y = "") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.placement = "outside",
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 90),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing.y = unit(0.4, "lines"),
        legend.position = "bottom")

Stack the season bar on top of the panels.

Builds a timestamp and keeps only the columns needed. parse_number() handles HOUR stored as text (e.g. “13:00”), and non-numeric COUNT values become NA.

    DATE = as_date(DATE),
    HOUR = parse_number(as.character(HOUR)),          # 0-23 as a number

    datetime = as.POSIXct(DATE, tz = "UTC") + HOUR * 3600   # hourly timestamp
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(datetime), !is.na(SEASON)) |>          # drop rows that failed to parse
  select(datetime, SEASON, CELL_ID, COUNT)
